decisions.choice: the word that came to Jeremiah: a heading that opens a new message
decisions.reason: The same heading opens the temple sermon (7:1) and the covenant sermon (11:1). What follows is a prose account of an acted lesson at a potter's workshop and the message drawn from it (verses 2-12). Poetry follows in verses 13-17, and verses 18-23 tell of a plot against Jeremiah and his prayer about it.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying: / This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD: / This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah:
decisions.reason: The book's fixed wording for this heading (as in 7:1 and 11:1). Balanced puts it as a plain statement and drops "saying", which only introduces the quotation; Readable says it more simply still.

decisions.choice: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte del SEÑOR, diciendo: / Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte del SEÑOR: / Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a Jeremías:
alternatives: La palabra que vino a Jeremías del SEÑOR
decisions.reason: The fixed Spanish wording of this heading in Jeremiah, used for the whole block. Literal keeps "diciendo", which only introduces the quotation; Balanced drops it, and Readable says who gave the message.

decisions.choice: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa BWANA, kusema: / Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa BWANA: / Huu ndio ujumbe ambao BWANA alimpa Yeremia:
decisions.reason: The fixed Swahili wording of this heading in Jeremiah at each level; Literal keeps "kusema" for the Hebrew "saying", Balanced and Readable drop it as the English does.

source.text: ק֥וּם וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֖מָּה אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת־דְּבָרָֽי׃

en.B: "Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words."
en.R: "Get up and go down to the potter's workshop. When you are there, I will give you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message."

es.L: «Levántate y desciende a la casa del alfarero, y allí te haré oír {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras».
es.B: «Levántate y baja a la casa del alfarero, y allí te haré oír {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras».
es.R: «Levántate y baja al taller del alfarero. Cuando estés allí, te daré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mensaje».

sw.L: "Ondoka, ushuke [mpaka] nyumba ya mfinyanzi, na huko nitakusikiza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.B: "Inuka, ushuke kwenda nyumbani kwa mfinyanzi, na huko nitakufanya uyasikie maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}."
sw.R: "Inuka, ushuke mpaka karakana ya mfinyanzi. Ukiwa huko, nitakupa ujumbe {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: the potter's house: the workshop where a potter shaped and fired clay pots
decisions.reason: Clay jars, bowls and lamps were the everyday containers of the ancient world, and potters worked near a supply of clay and water. Jeremiah "goes down" to the workshop, which suggests it lay below the temple and the upper city, perhaps near the Potsherd Gate that led out to the valley of Ben-hinnom (19:2).

decisions.choice: arise and go down: a call to set out at once
decisions.reason: "Arise" before another verb of motion urges the hearer to start doing it (13:4, 6). It does not mean that Jeremiah was lying or sitting down.

decisions.choice: there I will let you hear my words: the message will come at the workshop, through what Jeremiah sees
decisions.reason: God does not give the word first and then send Jeremiah to act it out. The lesson is given at the potter's house, after Jeremiah has watched the potter at work (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: the potter's workshop
decisions.reason: "House" here is a place of work. Readable says "workshop" so that young readers do not picture the potter's home.

decisions.choice: la casa del alfarero (Literal, Balanced); el taller del alfarero (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for the potter's workshop. Readable says "taller" so that the reader does not picture the potter's home, as the English Readable says "workshop".

decisions.choice: quotation marks « » for the LORD's words to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: In this prose account the LORD's words to Jeremiah are quoted as prose speech, as the English does; the message he is to pass on (verse 11) takes “ ” inside them.

decisions.choice: karakana ya mfinyanzi
decisions.reason: "House" here is a place of work, so Readable says "karakana" (workshop), as the English Readable says "workshop".

records.literal_gloss: And I went down [to the] house of the potter, and behold, he [was] doing work on the two stones.

en.L: So I went down to the potter's house, and look, he [was] doing work on the wheel.
en.B: So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
en.R: So I went down to the potter's workshop. I saw him there, working at his potter's wheel.

es.L: Y descendí a la casa del alfarero, y he aquí, él [estaba] haciendo un trabajo sobre la rueda.
es.B: Así que bajé a la casa del alfarero, y allí estaba él, trabajando en el torno.
es.R: Así que bajé al taller del alfarero. Lo vi allí, trabajando en su torno de alfarero.

sw.L: Basi nikashuka [mpaka] nyumba ya mfinyanzi, na tazama, yeye [alikuwa] akifanya kazi juu ya gurudumu.
sw.B: Basi nilishuka mpaka nyumbani kwa mfinyanzi, nami nikamwona akifanya kazi kwenye gurudumu lake.
sw.R: Basi nilishuka mpaka karakana ya mfinyanzi. Nikamwona huko akifanya kazi kwenye gurudumu lake la kufinyangia.

decisions.choice: the two stones: the potter's wheel, made of two discs
decisions.reason: The word means "a pair of stones". A potter's wheel had two discs joined by an upright shaft: the potter turned the lower one with his feet and shaped the clay on the upper one. The same word names the stones a woman sat on to give birth (Exodus 1:16), which were also a pair.

decisions.choice: look, he was doing work: the scene as Jeremiah came upon it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that draws attention puts the reader beside Jeremiah as he arrives and sees the potter already busy (as in 13:7). The written text joins the pronoun to that word; the text as read keeps them separate. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the wheel
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is one object, so every level says "wheel"; the literal form is given in meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there he was (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps a word that calls attention, as in 13:7. Balanced uses an English turn of phrase with the same effect, and Readable says "I saw".

decisions.choice: la rueda (Literal); el torno (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is the potter's wheel, made of two discs. Literal says "la rueda", as the English says "the wheel"; Balanced and Readable use "torno", the ordinary Spanish word for a potter's wheel.

decisions.choice: gurudumu
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "two stones" is the potter's wheel, so every level says "gurudumu"; Readable adds "la kufinyangia" (for shaping clay).

source.text: וְנִשְׁחַ֣ת הַכְּלִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֛ה בַּחֹ֖מֶר בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֗ב וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ כְּלִ֣י אַחֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשַׁ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י הַיּוֹצֵ֖ר לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And was spoiled the vessel that he [was] making in the clay in [the] hand of the potter, and he again made it another vessel, as was right in [the] eyes of the potter to do.

en.L: And the vessel that he was making of clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, and he made it again into another vessel, as it was right in the eyes of the potter to do.
en.B: If the pot he was shaping from the clay went wrong in the potter's hand, he would make it over into another pot, whatever seemed best to him.
en.R: Sometimes the pot he was shaping from the clay did not turn out well in his hands. Then he would shape the clay into another pot, in whatever way he thought best.

es.L: Y la vasija que él hacía de barro se echó a perder en la mano del alfarero, y él volvió a hacer de ella otra vasija, según le pareció bien a los ojos del alfarero hacer.
es.B: Si la vasija que estaba moldeando con el barro se le estropeaba en la mano, el alfarero hacía con ella otra vasija, como mejor le parecía.
es.R: A veces la vasija que moldeaba con el barro no le salía bien. Entonces él volvía a moldear el barro y hacía otra vasija, como a él le parecía mejor.

sw.L: Na chombo alichokuwa akikifanya kwa udongo kikaharibika mkononi mwa mfinyanzi, naye akakifanya tena kuwa chombo kingine, kama ilivyokuwa sawa machoni pa mfinyanzi kufanya.
sw.B: Kila mara chungu alichokuwa akikifinyanga kwa udongo kilipoharibika mkononi mwake, alikifanya upya kuwa chungu kingine, kama alivyoona vema yeye mwenyewe.
sw.R: Wakati mwingine chungu alichokuwa akikifinyanga hakikutoka vizuri mikononi mwake. Ndipo alipoufinyanga udongo ule kuwa chungu kingine, kwa namna yoyote aliyoona ni bora.

decisions.choice: was spoiled ... and he made it again: what the potter did whenever a pot went wrong
decisions.reason: The verb forms can describe something that happened again and again. Jeremiah watched the potter at work, and the lesson in verse 6 is about what a potter is able to do, so the verse is best read as his usual practice. It could also tell of one pot that Jeremiah saw spoiled and reshaped; the lesson is the same.

decisions.choice: spoiled: ruined, no longer fit for its purpose
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the ruined loincloth (13:7, 9). Here the ruin is not final: the potter still has the clay in his hand and can make something new from it.

decisions.choice: as was right in the eyes of the potter: as the potter himself judged best
decisions.reason: "Right in someone's eyes" means what seems good to that person. The new pot is made to the potter's own design, not to the clay's. The phrase prepares for the question of verse 6.

decisions.choice: pot
decisions.reason: The word means any vessel or container. Since this one is made of clay on a potter's wheel, Balanced and Readable say "pot"; Literal keeps "vessel".

decisions.choice: If ... / Sometimes ... Then ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the repeated action described in meaning decision m1 with "if ... would" and "sometimes ... then".

decisions.choice: Si ... se le estropeaba ... hacía (Balanced); A veces ... Entonces ... volvía a moldear (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the Spanish imperfect to show the potter's usual practice (meaning decision m1), as the English uses "would" and "sometimes". Literal keeps the preterite of a single event.

decisions.choice: chungu
decisions.reason: The vessel is a clay pot made on the wheel, so Balanced and Readable say "chungu"; Literal keeps the general "chombo".

records.literal_gloss: Like the potter this not can I do to you, house of Israel? declares Yahweh. Behold, like the clay in [the] hand of the potter, so you [are] in my hand, house of Israel.

en.L: "Can I not do with you as this potter [does], house of Israel? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Look, like the clay in the potter's hand, so [are] you in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, house of Israel.
en.B: "House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. As the clay is in the potter's hand, so you are in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, house of Israel.
en.R: "People of Israel, can I not do with you what this potter does? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You are in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands just as the clay is in the potter's hands.

sw.R: "Watu wa Israeli, je, siwezi kuwafanyia kama mfinyanzi huyu anavyofanya? anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ninyi mko mikononi {{deity_pronoun:mwangu|Mwangu}} kama udongo ulivyo mikononi mwa mfinyanzi.

decisions.choice: can I not do: a question that expects the answer "yes, you can"
decisions.reason: The question is a strong way of saying that God has the same power over Israel that the potter has over his clay. The comparison is with the potter's action, not with his skill: what he does with a spoiled pot (verse 4).

decisions.choice: like the clay in the potter's hand: Israel's future is in God's hands, and he is free to reshape it
decisions.reason: The picture is of God's rule over his people. Verses 7-10 show that this freedom is not whim: God reshapes a nation in answer to how it turns, toward evil or away from it. The picture can be read both as a warning (the people can be reworked) and as hope (spoiled clay is not thrown away).

decisions.choice: the potter and the clay: a picture Isaiah also uses
decisions.reason: Isaiah speaks of the clay that cannot question the potter (Isaiah 29:16; 45:9) and of God as the potter and his people as the clay (Isaiah 64:7). Paul draws on the picture when he writes of God's freedom in Romans 9:20-21.

decisions.choice: People of Israel
decisions.reason: "House of Israel" means the people descended from Israel. Readable says "people" and names them once.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD in the middle of the question
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the formula after the question and before the picture of the clay; every level keeps it there, as Isaiah's wording does.

decisions.choice: declara el SEÑOR (Literal); afirma el SEÑOR (Balanced); dice el SEÑOR (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Spanish wording of neʾum YHWH for the whole block, always after a comma. Here it stands after the question, as in the Hebrew, so the question mark comes before the comma.

decisions.choice: plural you: {{plural_you:con ustedes|con vosotros}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" in the block is a plural_you span, Latin American "ustedes" by default with "vosotros" as the alternative, covering the pronoun or verb that changes. Here God speaks to the whole house of Israel.

decisions.choice: asema BWANA (Literal, Balanced); anasema BWANA (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili wording of the formula "declares the LORD" (2 Kings 19:33), kept in the middle of the question where the Hebrew has it.

source.text: רֶ֣גַע אֲדַבֵּ֔ר עַל־גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־מַמְלָכָ֑ה לִנְת֥וֹשׁ וְלִנְת֖וֹץ וּֽלְהַאֲבִֽיד׃

en.L: At one moment I may speak concerning a nation or concerning a kingdom, to uproot and to tear down and to destroy [it],
en.B: At one time I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, that I will uproot it, tear it down and destroy it,
en.R: Sometimes I may announce that I will uproot a nation or a kingdom, tear it down and destroy it.

es.L: En un momento puedo hablar acerca de una nación o acerca de un reino, para arrancar, para derribar y para destruir,
es.B: En un momento puedo hablar acerca de una nación o de un reino, diciendo que la arrancaré, la derribaré y la destruiré;
es.R: A veces puedo anunciar que voy a arrancar una nación o un reino, que voy a derribarlo y destruirlo.

sw.L: Wakati mmoja naweza kusema juu ya taifa au juu ya ufalme, kuling'oa na kulibomoa na kuliangamiza,
sw.B: Wakati fulani naweza kusema kuhusu taifa au ufalme kwamba nitaling'oa, nitalibomoa na kuliangamiza,
sw.R: Wakati mwingine naweza kutangaza kwamba nitang'oa taifa au ufalme fulani, nitalibomoa na kuliangamiza.

decisions.choice: to uproot and to tear down and to destroy: the words of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are three of the four words of judgment in 1:10, where God set Jeremiah over nations and kingdoms. Verse 9 takes up the two words of restoration. Here God explains how that call works: the word he speaks over a nation is not the last word, because the nation's response matters (verses 8 and 10).

decisions.choice: at one moment: at any time
decisions.reason: The word means an instant. With its partner in verse 9 it means "at one time ... at another time": whenever God speaks a word of judgment or of blessing.

decisions.choice: a nation or a kingdom: any nation, not only Israel
decisions.reason: The rule is stated for all peoples, as in 1:10, before it is applied to Judah in verse 11. Jonah 3 shows it at work for Nineveh.

decisions.choice: uproot, tear down, destroy
decisions.reason: The same English verbs as in 1:10 at every level, so the reader hears the echo.

decisions.choice: may speak / may announce
decisions.reason: The verb describes something that can happen at any time, so English adds "may". Literal and Balanced end with a comma because the sentence runs on into verse 8; Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: arrancar, derribar, destruir
decisions.reason: The same Spanish verbs at every level each time the words of Jeremiah's call (1:10) return, so the reader hears the echo; verse 9 adds "edificar" and "plantar".

decisions.choice: kung'oa, kubomoa, kuangamiza
decisions.reason: The same Swahili verbs as Jeremiah's call (1:10) at every level, so the reader hears the echo; verse 9 adds "kujenga" and "kupanda".

decisions.choice: I will relent: God turns from the judgment he announced when the nation turns from its evil
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used when God relented after Moses pleaded for Israel (Exodus 32:14), where its sense is explained. It does not mean that God was wrong or that he changes as people do (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29). These verses show that God's warnings are meant to bring people back: when a nation turns, God turns too. Jonah 3:10 tells of exactly this, and Jeremiah 26:3 and 26:13 apply it to Judah.

decisions.choice: its evil ... the evil that I planned: wrongdoing and the disaster that answers it
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word stands for both. The nation's evil is its wickedness; the evil God plans is the harm or disaster of judgment. The repetition shows the one answering the other.

decisions.choice: against which I have spoken: the nation, not its evil, is what God spoke about
decisions.reason: The words "which I spoke against it" refer back to the nation of verse 7, over which God has spoken words of judgment.

decisions.choice: planned: devised, intended
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a craftsman's designs as well as of plans. It returns in verse 11, where God says he is devising a plan against Judah, and in verse 18, where the people make plans against Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: relent (Literal, Balanced); change my mind (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 32:14. "Repent" is avoided at every level, since in English it suggests turning from sin.

decisions.choice: disaster
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "evil" twice, as the Hebrew does. Balanced and Readable say "disaster" for the second, so that God is not heard planning wickedness (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: me retractaré (Literal); desistiré (Balanced); cambiaré de parecer (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb of God relenting (nicham). It is never "arrepentirse" here, which in Spanish suggests turning from sin (meaning decision m1; 1 Samuel 15 as published). Literal says "retractarse", as in 4:28 and 15:6; Balanced and Readable say he holds back or changes his mind.

decisions.choice: el desastre
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "mal" for both Hebrew words, as the Hebrew does; Balanced and Readable say "desastre" for the harm God planned (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: nitaghairi (Literal, Balanced); nitabadili nia yangu (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Kughairi" is to call off what one intended; "kutubu" is avoided because it means repenting of sin.

decisions.choice: to build and to plant: the two words of restoration in 1:10
decisions.reason: After the words of judgment in verse 7, these are the last two words of Jeremiah's call (1:10). They return as promises in 24:6 and 31:28.

decisions.choice: another
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "a moment". English says "at another moment" or "at another time" to show the contrast with verse 7.

decisions.choice: build up
decisions.reason: The same verb "build" as in 1:10. Readable adds "up", which English uses when a nation is made strong.

decisions.choice: otro momento / Otras veces
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "a moment"; Spanish says "en otro momento" to show the contrast with verse 7.

records.literal_gloss: and it does the evil in my eyes, not listening to my voice, and I will relent concerning the good that I said to do good [to] it.

en.L: and it does the evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, not listening to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, then I will relent concerning the good that I said I would do for it.

es.L: y hace lo malo ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos, no escuchando {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, entonces me retractaré del bien que dije que le haría.

decisions.choice: I will relent concerning the good: God's promises are also bound up with the people's response
decisions.reason: As in verse 8 (meaning decision m1 there), God relents, but this time from good he had promised. A promise of blessing is no shelter for a nation that turns to evil, just as a threat of judgment is not the end for one that turns from it.

decisions.choice: not listening to my voice: not obeying
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice means to do what he says (7:23, 28; 11:4, 7).

decisions.choice: the evil in my eyes: what God judges to be evil
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means in God's judgment, as in the formula of Judges and Kings, "did what was evil in the sight of the LORD".

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the good I said I would do". Balanced and Readable say "promised", which is what such a word of blessing is.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אֱמָר־נָ֣א אֶל־אִישׁ־יְהוּדָה֩ וְעַל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה וְחֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א אִ֚ישׁ מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהֵיטִ֥יבוּ דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם וּמַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, say, please, to [the] man of Judah and to [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, Thus says Yahweh: Behold, I [am] forming against you evil and devising against you a plan. Turn, please, each from his way the evil, and make good your ways and your deeds.

en.L: And now, speak to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am shaping evil against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each one from {{gender:their|his}} evil way, and make good your ways and your deeds.'
en.B: So now, say to {{gender:the people|the men}} of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am shaping disaster for you and making plans against you. Turn back, every one of you, from your evil way, and change your ways and your actions for the better.'
en.R: So now go and tell the people of Judah and everyone who lives in Jerusalem, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Like a potter, I am shaping disaster for you. I am making plans against you. So each of you must turn away from your evil way of life. Change the way you live and the things you do.'

es.L: Y ahora, habla, te ruego, a {{gender:la gente de Judá|los hombres de Judá}} y a los habitantes de Jerusalén, diciendo: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo estoy formando un mal contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y trazando un plan contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, cada uno de su mal camino, y {{plural_you:mejoren sus caminos y sus obras|mejorad vuestros caminos y vuestras obras}}”.
es.B: Así que ahora, di a {{gender:la gente de Judá|los hombres de Judá}} y a los que viven en Jerusalén: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Estoy formando un desastre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y haciendo planes contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}}, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de su mal camino, y {{plural_you:mejoren su manera de vivir y sus acciones|mejorad vuestra manera de vivir y vuestras acciones}}”.
es.R: Así que ahora ve y diles a la gente de Judá y a todos los que viven en Jerusalén: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Como un alfarero, estoy formando un desastre para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Estoy haciendo planes contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Así que cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:tiene|ha}} que dejar su mal camino. {{plural_you:Cambien su manera de vivir y lo que hacen|Cambiad vuestra manera de vivir y lo que hacéis}}”.

sw.L: Basi sasa, sema na watu wa Yuda na wakazi wa Yerusalemu, ukisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, ninawafinyangia mabaya, na kuwawazia mpango juu yenu. Rudini, kila mmoja kutoka njia yake mbaya, mkazitengeneze njia zenu na matendo yenu.'
sw.B: Basi sasa, waambie watu wa Yuda na wakazi wa Yerusalemu, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninawafinyangia maafa na kufanya mipango dhidi yenu. Rudini, kila mmoja wenu, aache njia yake mbaya; zifanyeni njia zenu na matendo yenu kuwa mema.'
sw.R: Basi sasa nenda ukawaambie watu wa Yuda na wote wanaoishi Yerusalemu, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Kama mfinyanzi, ninawafinyangia maafa. Ninafanya mipango dhidi yenu. Kwa hiyo kila mmoja wenu na aiache njia yake mbaya ya maisha. Badilisheni jinsi mnavyoishi na mambo mnayoyafanya.'

decisions.choice: shaping: forming, the potter's own verb
decisions.reason: The word for "shaping" is the same as the word for "potter" in verses 2-6, which means "one who shapes". God speaks of himself as the potter at work on Judah: the disaster is being formed, not yet fired, and verses 7-8 have just said that it can still be turned aside.

decisions.choice: man of Judah: the people of Judah as a whole
decisions.reason: The singular noun "man" with a place name is a collective way of naming all the people of a land, as in 11:2.

decisions.choice: make good your ways and your deeds: change your conduct for the better
decisions.reason: The same call as in the temple sermon (7:3, 5) and in 26:13. "Ways" is the whole course of life, and "deeds" the things done along it.

decisions.choice: please ... now: an urging word, softening the command
decisions.reason: The little word joined to "say" and to "turn" makes the commands earnest appeals. Even while the disaster is being shaped, God pleads with the people to turn.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah, with "the men of Judah" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective means the whole people, so the inclusive form is the default, as in 11:2. Readable says "the people", which needs no alternative. In Literal "each one from their evil way" has "his" as the alternative for the same reason.

decisions.choice: Like a potter
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with the potter plain, since the shared Hebrew word (meaning decision m1) cannot be heard in English.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The message Jeremiah is to give is quoted inside the LORD's speech to him, which began in verse 6, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Así dice el SEÑOR: / El SEÑOR dice esto: / Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR:
decisions.reason: The Spanish wording of "Thus says the LORD" for the whole block, followed by a colon, as in the Kings and Chronicles note.

decisions.choice: la gente de Judá, with "los hombres de Judá" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew collective "man of Judah" means the whole people (meaning decision m2), so the inclusive form is the default, as the published Spanish has it elsewhere.

decisions.choice: ninawafinyangia
decisions.reason: Swahili "kufinyanga" (to shape clay) shares its root with "mfinyanzi" (potter), just as the Hebrew verb shares its root with "potter", so the wordplay of meaning decision m1 can be heard at every level.

decisions.choice: BWANA asema hivi: / Hivi ndivyo BWANA asemavyo: / Hili ndilo BWANA analosema:
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili wording of "Thus says the LORD" at each level (2 Kings 19:6; 1 Chronicles 17:4). "Watu wa Yuda" is already inclusive, so Swahili needs no gender alternative here.

source.text: וְאָמְר֖וּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ כִּֽי־אַחֲרֵ֤י מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ וְאִ֛ישׁ שְׁרִר֥וּת לִבּֽוֹ־הָרָ֖ע נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And they will say, Hopeless! For after our plans we will walk, and each [the] stubbornness of his heart the evil we will do.

en.L: But they will say, 'It is hopeless! For we will walk after our own plans, and we will act, each one according to the stubbornness of {{gender:their|his}} evil heart.'"
en.B: But they will say, 'It is no use! We will follow our own plans; each of us will act in the stubbornness of our evil hearts.'"
en.R: But they will answer, 'It is no use! We will do what we have planned. Each of us will stubbornly follow our own evil heart.'"

es.L: Pero ellos dirán: “¡Es inútil! Porque iremos tras nuestros propios planes, y cada uno hará según la terquedad de su corazón malvado”».
es.B: Pero ellos dirán: “¡No sirve de nada! Seguiremos nuestros propios planes; cada uno de nosotros actuará según la terquedad de su corazón malvado”».
es.R: Pero ellos responderán: “¡No sirve de nada! Haremos lo que hemos planeado. Cada uno de nosotros seguirá tercamente lo que le dicte su corazón malvado”».

sw.L: Lakini watasema, 'Hakuna tumaini! Kwa maana tutafuata mipango yetu wenyewe, na kila mmoja atatenda kwa ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya.'"
sw.B: Lakini watasema, 'Haifai kitu! Tutafuata mipango yetu wenyewe; kila mmoja wetu atatenda kwa ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya.'"
sw.R: Lakini watajibu, 'Haifai kitu! Tutafanya yale tuliyopanga. Kila mmoja wetu atafuata kwa ukaidi moyo wake mbaya.'"

decisions.choice: hopeless: it is no use, we have given up
decisions.reason: The word means that something is past hope. The people do not mean that they cannot turn but that they will not: there is no point in asking them (as in 2:25). It is despair turned into defiance.

decisions.choice: they will say: God tells Jeremiah in advance how the people will answer
decisions.reason: The verb looks ahead. Before Jeremiah has spoken, God knows the reply, and the oracle of verses 13-17 answers it.

decisions.choice: our plans ... the stubbornness of his evil heart: they will follow their own designs, not God's
decisions.reason: "Plans" is the word God used for his own plan in verse 11, so the people set their plans against his. "The stubbornness of the heart" is Jeremiah's phrase for a will set hard against God (7:24; 11:8; 13:10); the heart is the seat of thought and will.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of his evil heart / ... of our evil hearts / stubbornly follow our own evil heart
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this phrase in Jeremiah, turned into the first person because the people speak of themselves. The gender setting in Literal gives "his" as the alternative for "each one ... their".

decisions.choice: closing quotation marks
decisions.reason: The people's reply ends the message Jeremiah is to give and the LORD's speech that began in verse 6.

decisions.choice: la terquedad de su corazón malvado (Literal, Balanced); seguirá tercamente (Readable)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's phrase for a will set hard against God keeps one Spanish wording through the block, as the English keeps "stubbornness".

decisions.choice: ukaidi wa moyo wake mbaya / kwa ukaidi
decisions.reason: "Ukaidi" (stubborn defiance) is used for Jeremiah's phrase throughout this block; "ugumu wa moyo" suggests hardness rather than wilful refusal.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַֽׁאֲלוּ־נָא֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם מִ֥י שָׁמַ֖ע כָּאֵ֑לֶּה שַֽׁעֲרֻרִת֙ עָשְׂתָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: Ask, please, among the nations, who has heard like these? A horrible thing she has done exceedingly, [the] virgin of Israel.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Ask among the nations, \q who has heard [anything] like these [things]? \q The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Ask among the nations, \q who has ever heard of such things? \q The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: \q Ask the other nations \q if anyone has ever heard of something like this. \q Israel should be like a pure young woman, \q but she has done something truly horrible.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q {{plural_you:Pregunten|Preguntad}} entre las naciones, \q ¿quién ha oído [cosas] como estas? \q Algo muy horrible ha hecho la virgen de Israel.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: \q {{plural_you:Pregunten|Preguntad}} entre las naciones: \q ¿Quién ha oído alguna vez cosa semejante? \q La virgen Israel ha hecho algo horrendo.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q {{plural_you:Pregúntenles|Preguntadles}} a las otras naciones \q si alguien ha oído alguna vez algo así. \q Israel debía ser como una joven pura, \q pero ha hecho algo verdaderamente horrible.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: \q Ulizeni kati ya mataifa, \q ni nani aliyesikia [mambo] kama haya? \q Bikira wa Israeli amefanya jambo la kuchukiza mno.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: \q Ulizeni kati ya mataifa, \q ni nani aliyewahi kusikia mambo kama haya? \q Bikira Israeli amefanya jambo la kutisha mno.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: \q Yaulizeni mataifa mengine \q kama kuna mtu aliyewahi kusikia jambo kama hili. \q Israeli alipaswa kuwa kama msichana safi, \q lakini amefanya jambo la kutisha kweli.

decisions.choice: therefore: the oracle answers the people's refusal in verse 12
decisions.reason: After the prose lesson of verses 1-12, the LORD speaks in poetry (verses 13-17) about the people who said they would follow their own plans. As elsewhere in the prophets, his words in poetry are not set in quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the virgin of Israel: the nation pictured as a young unmarried woman
decisions.reason: The picture speaks of what Israel was meant to be: young, cherished and faithful to one husband, the LORD (2:2, 32). The shock is that she has acted in a way that no other nation has (2:10-11). The same title returns in hope in 31:4 and 31:21.

decisions.choice: a horrible thing: something shocking and revolting
decisions.reason: The word is used of what makes people shudder (5:30; 23:14; Hosea 6:10). The nations are called as witnesses, because even they would not do such a thing (2:10-11).

decisions.choice: Israel should be like a pure young woman, but
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of meaning decision m2, which young readers would miss in the bare title "virgin of Israel".

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: / The LORD says this: / This is what the LORD says:
decisions.reason: The fixed wording for this formula, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable say "So" or "Therefore" for the word that ties it to verse 12.

decisions.choice: la virgen de Israel (Literal); la virgen Israel (Balanced); como una joven pura (Readable)
decisions.reason: The nation pictured as a young unmarried woman (meaning decision m2). Readable spells out the picture, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for the oracle
decisions.reason: As in the English, the LORD's poetry spoken through the prophet takes no quotation marks; speech quoted inside an oracle does.

decisions.choice: Bikira wa Israeli (Literal); Bikira Israeli (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Bikira" keeps the picture of the young unmarried woman; Readable spells it out as "msichana safi", as the English Readable does.

source.text: הֲיַעֲזֹ֥ב מִצּ֛וּר שָׂדַ֖י שֶׁ֣לֶג לְבָנ֑וֹן אִם־יִנָּתְשׁ֗וּ מַ֛יִם זָרִ֥ים קָרִ֖ים נוֹזְלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Does leave from [the] rock of [the] field [the] snow of Lebanon? Or are plucked up waters strange, cold, flowing?

sw.L: Je, theluji ya Lebanoni huondoka kwenye mwamba wa porini? \q Au maji mageni, baridi, yatiririkayo hung'olewa?
sw.B: Je, theluji ya Lebanoni huwahi kutoweka kutoka vilele vyake vya miamba? \q Je, vijito vya baridi vitiririkavyo kutoka mbali huwahi kukatika?
sw.R: Je, theluji huwahi kutoweka kwenye vilele vya miamba vya Lebanoni? \q Je, vijito vya maji baridi vinavyotiririka kutoka mbali huwahi kuacha kutiririka?

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The snow on the high mountains of Lebanon lasts all year, and the streams fed by it keep flowing. Nature stays true to its course; the next verse sets Israel's unfaithfulness against it. This is the plain sense, though the details of the verse are hard to read.

decisions.choice: the rock of the field: the rocky slopes or heights of the open country
alternatives: from the rock of the Almighty
decisions.reason: The words are "the rock of the field", which may mean the rocky high ground of Lebanon itself. With a small change of letters some read a name, such as Sirion (Mount Hermon, Deuteronomy 3:9), or "the rock of the Almighty". The meaning of the whole verse stays much the same.

decisions.choice: are the strange, cold, flowing waters plucked up: do the cold streams from far away ever fail
decisions.reason: The verb means to be pulled up or torn away, an odd word for water; with two letters exchanged it would mean "dry up". "Strange" usually means foreign; here it may mean waters that come from far off, or, with one letter changed, "from the mountains". The point is that these streams never stop.

decisions.choice: ever cut off / ever stop; that flow from far away
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of meaning decision m3 in plain words and add "ever" to show that the questions expect "no" (m1).

source.text: כִּֽי־שְׁכֵחֻ֥נִי עַמִּ֖י לַשָּׁ֣וְא יְקַטֵּ֑רוּ וַיַּכְשִׁל֤וּם בְּדַרְכֵיהֶם֙ שְׁבִילֵ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם לָלֶ֣כֶת נְתִיב֔וֹת דֶּ֖רֶךְ לֹ֥א סְלוּלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For have forgotten me my people; to worthlessness they burn incense, and they have made them stumble in their ways, [the] paths of antiquity, to walk [in] bypaths, a road not built up,

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; they burn incense to worthlessness, \q and they have made them stumble in their ways, the ancient roads, \q to walk on bypaths, a road not built up,
en.B: Yet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; they make offerings of incense to worthless gods, \q which have made them stumble in their ways, on the ancient roads, \q so that they walk on side paths, on a road that is not built up,
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They burn incense to useless idols. \q These idols have made them stumble on the old, well-known roads. \q Now they walk on side paths, on rough roads that no one has built.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha olvidado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo; queman incienso a la vanidad, \q y los han hecho tropezar en sus caminos, las sendas antiguas, \q para andar por veredas, un camino no allanado,
es.B: Sin embargo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha olvidado; ofrecen incienso a dioses vanos, \q que los han hecho tropezar en sus caminos, en las sendas antiguas, \q para que anden por senderos, por un camino sin allanar,
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha olvidado. Queman incienso a ídolos inútiles. \q Esos ídolos los han hecho tropezar en los caminos antiguos y conocidos. \q Ahora andan por senderos, por caminos ásperos que nadie ha preparado.

sw.L: Lakini watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamenisahau; wanafukiza uvumba kwa ubatili, \q nao wamewakwaza katika njia zao, njia za zamani, \q ili watembee katika vijia, njia isiyotengenezwa,
sw.B: Hata hivyo watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamenisahau; wanafukiza uvumba kwa miungu isiyofaa kitu, \q ambayo imewakwaza katika njia zao, katika njia za zamani, \q hata wanatembea katika vijia vya pembeni, katika njia isiyotengenezwa,
sw.R: Lakini watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamenisahau. Wanafukiza uvumba kwa sanamu zisizo na faida. \q Sanamu hizo zimewakwaza katika njia za zamani zinazojulikana. \q Sasa wanatembea katika vijia vya pembeni, katika njia mbovu ambazo hakuna aliyezitengeneza.

decisions.choice: worthlessness: emptiness, the false gods that are nothing
decisions.reason: The word means what is empty, false or useless. Here it stands for the idols, which have nothing in them to help (2:5; 10:15; 16:19).

decisions.choice: they have made them stumble: the worthless gods have tripped up the people
alternatives: those who led them astray have made them stumble
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It most naturally refers to the worthless gods just named; it may also mean those who led the people to them, such as false prophets (23:13). Either way the people have been led off the right road.

decisions.choice: the ancient roads: the old, good way of faithfulness to the LORD
decisions.reason: God had told the people to ask for "the paths of long ago" and walk in the good way (6:16). They have left those tried roads for rough tracks of their own.

decisions.choice: a road not built up: a rough track, not a proper highway
decisions.reason: A main road was built up with earth and stones so that it was raised, level and clear (Isaiah 57:14; 62:10). A road "not built up" is uneven and easy to stumble on. The sentence runs on into verse 16.

decisions.choice: worthless gods, which ... / useless idols. These idols ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the worthless things are false gods and make them the subject of "made them stumble", following meaning decisions m1 and m2.

decisions.choice: dioses vanos, que ... / ídolos inútiles. Esos ídolos ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "worthlessness" names the false gods (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say so, and make the gods the subject of "hacer tropezar", as the English does.

source.text: לָשׂ֥וּם אַרְצָ֛ם לְשַׁמָּ֖ה שְׁרִיק֣וֹתעוֹלָ֑ם כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשֹּׁ֖ם וְיָנִ֥יד בְּרֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: to make their land a horror, hissings forever; every one passing by it will be appalled and will shake with his head.

en.L: to make their land a horror, a hissing forever; \q everyone who passes by it will be appalled and shake {{gender:their|his}} head.
en.B: making their land a horror, an object of scorn forever; \q all who pass by it will be appalled and shake their heads.
en.R: So their land will become a horror, something people mock forever. \q Everyone who passes by will be shocked and will shake their heads.

es.L: para hacer de su tierra un horror, una burla para siempre; \q todo el que pase por ella se asombrará y meneará la cabeza.
es.B: convirtiendo su tierra en un horror, en objeto de burla para siempre; \q todos los que pasen por ella se espantarán y menearán la cabeza.
es.R: Así su tierra se convertirá en un horror, en algo de lo que la gente se burlará para siempre. \q Todos los que pasen por allí se quedarán espantados y menearán la cabeza.

sw.L: kuifanya nchi yao kuwa kitisho, [kitu cha] kuzomewa milele; \q kila apitaye karibu nayo atashangaa na kutikisa kichwa chake.
sw.B: wakiifanya nchi yao kuwa kitisho, kitu cha kudharauliwa milele; \q wote wapitao karibu nayo watashangaa na kutikisa vichwa vyao.
sw.R: Hivyo nchi yao itakuwa kitisho, kitu ambacho watu hukidhihaki milele. \q Kila mtu atakayepita karibu nayo atashtuka na kutikisa kichwa.

decisions.choice: to make: the result of their wandering, the end to which it leads
decisions.reason: The form often expresses purpose, but here it gives the outcome: by leaving the good road the people bring ruin on their own land. It is not that they meant to.

decisions.choice: a hissing: a whistle of shock and scorn at a ruin
decisions.reason: People who passed a destroyed place whistled or hissed in amazement and contempt (19:8; 1 Kings 9:8; Lamentations 2:15). The written text and the text as read differ by one letter in this word; both mean "hissing".

decisions.choice: shake the head: a gesture of horror and mockery
decisions.reason: Shaking the head over someone's fall expresses both dismay and scorn (Psalm 22:8; Lamentations 2:15).

decisions.choice: horror, hissing / horror, object of scorn / horror, something people mock
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this pair in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: their head, with "his head" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: "Everyone who passes by" means men and women alike, so Literal's "his" becomes "their" by default. Balanced and Readable say "all ... their heads", which needs no alternative.

decisions.choice: un horror, una burla (Literal); un horror, objeto de burla (Balanced); un horror, algo de lo que la gente se burlará (Readable)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's lists of horror and hissing keep one Spanish wording through the block. The hissing (*shereqah*) is a whistle of scorn at a ruin; Spanish has no matching gesture, so even Literal says "burla", with the gesture explained in meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: kitisho, [kitu cha] kuzomewa / kitisho, kitu cha kudharauliwa / kitisho, kitu ambacho watu hukidhihaki
decisions.reason: The wording used for this list throughout Jeremiah: Literal keeps the hissing ("kuzomewa", jeered at), Balanced and Readable say what it expresses; the verb *sharaq* is "kuzomea" (L), "kuzomea kwa dharau" (B), "kudhihaki" (R). "Kila apitaye ... kichwa chake" needs no gender alternative in Swahili.

source.text: כְּרֽוּחַ־קָדִ֥ים אֲפִיצֵ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב עֹ֧רֶף וְלֹֽא־פָנִ֛ים אֶרְאֵ֖ם בְּי֥וֹם אֵידָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Like a wind of [the] east I will scatter them before [the] enemy; [the] back and not [the] face I will show them in [the] day of their calamity.

en.L: Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy; \q I will show them [the] back and not [the] face in the day of their calamity.
en.B: Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy; \q I will show them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} back, not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face, on the day of their disaster.
en.R: I will scatter them in front of their enemies, as the east wind scatters dust. \q On the day disaster strikes them, I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} back on them. I will not turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face toward them.

es.L: Como el viento del oriente los esparciré delante del enemigo; \q [la] espalda y no [el] rostro les mostraré en el día de su calamidad.
es.B: Como el viento del este los dispersaré delante del enemigo; \q les mostraré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} espalda y no {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro el día de su desgracia.
es.R: Los dispersaré delante de sus enemigos, como el viento del este dispersa el polvo. \q El día en que les llegue el desastre, les daré la espalda. \q No volveré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro hacia ellos.

sw.L: Kama upepo wa mashariki nitawatawanya mbele ya adui; \q nitawaonyesha kisogo wala si uso katika siku ya msiba wao.
sw.B: Kama upepo wa mashariki nitawatawanya mbele ya adui; \q nitawaonyesha mgongo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, si uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, siku ya maafa yao.
sw.R: Nitawatawanya mbele ya adui zao, kama upepo wa mashariki unavyotawanya mavumbi. \q Siku maafa yatakapowapata, nitawageuzia mgongo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. \q Sitawaelekezea uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.

decisions.choice: the east wind: the hot, dry wind off the desert
decisions.reason: The east wind blows in from the desert, withering plants and driving dust before it (4:11; 13:24). The people will be blown away before their enemy as dust and chaff are blown by it.

decisions.choice: show them the back and not the face: turn away from them and refuse help
decisions.reason: To turn the face toward someone is to look on him with favor and help him; to turn the back is to reject him. The people did this to God (2:27; 32:33), and now God will do it to them on the day they need him. With other vowels the letters could read "I will look on them with my back, not my face"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the day of their calamity: the day disaster overtakes them
decisions.reason: The word means a crushing disaster, the ruin that falls on a people or a person (46:21; 48:16; Proverbs 1:26-27).

decisions.choice: [the] back ... [the] face
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no "the" or "my" here. Literal adds the article in brackets; Balanced says "my back, not my face", which is the meaning.

decisions.choice: as the east wind scatters dust; turn my back on them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the east wind scatters and uses the English phrase "turn my back on", which carries the same picture as the Hebrew (meaning decision m2).

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לְכ֨וּ וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה עַֽל־יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ כִּי֩ לֹא־תֹאבַ֨ד תּוֹרָ֜ה מִכֹּהֵ֗ן וְעֵצָה֙ מֵֽחָכָ֔ם וְדָבָ֖ר מִנָּבִ֑יא לְכוּ֙ וְנַכֵּ֣הוּ בַלָּשׁ֔וֹן וְאַל־נַקְשִׁ֖יבָה אֶל־כָּל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Come and let us devise against Jeremiah plans, for not will perish instruction from [the] priest, and counsel from [the] wise, and [the] word from [the] prophet. Come and let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not pay attention to any of his words.

en.L: Then they said, "Come, and let us devise plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, and let us strike him with the tongue, and let us not pay attention to any of his words."
en.B: Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah. Instruction will never be lost to the priest, or counsel to the wise, or the word to the prophet. Come, let us attack him with words and pay no attention to anything he says."
en.R: Then some of the people said, "Come on, let us make plans against Jeremiah. We will still have priests to give us teaching, wise people to give us advice, and prophets to give us God's message. Come, let us attack him with our words. We will not listen to anything he says."

es.L: Entonces dijeron: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, y tramemos planes contra Jeremías, porque no faltará la instrucción al sacerdote, ni el consejo al sabio, ni la palabra al profeta. {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, y hirámoslo con la lengua, y no prestemos atención a ninguna de sus palabras».
es.B: Entonces dijeron: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, hagamos planes contra Jeremías. Nunca faltará la instrucción del sacerdote, ni el consejo del sabio, ni la palabra del profeta. {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, ataquémoslo con palabras y no hagamos caso de nada de lo que diga».
es.R: Entonces algunos del pueblo dijeron: «Vamos, hagamos planes contra Jeremías. Seguiremos teniendo sacerdotes que nos enseñen, sabios que nos aconsejen y profetas que nos den el mensaje de Dios. Vamos, ataquémoslo con nuestras palabras. No escucharemos nada de lo que diga».

sw.L: Ndipo wakasema, "Njooni, tufanye mipango dhidi ya Yeremia, kwa maana sheria haitapotea kwa kuhani, wala shauri kwa mwenye hekima, wala neno kwa nabii. Njooni, tumpige kwa ulimi, wala tusiyasikilize maneno yake yoyote."
sw.B: Ndipo wakasema, "Njooni, tufanye mipango dhidi ya Yeremia. Mafundisho hayatakosekana kwa kuhani, wala shauri kwa wenye hekima, wala neno kwa nabii. Njooni, tumshambulie kwa maneno, tusijali lolote analosema."
sw.R: Ndipo baadhi ya watu wakasema, "Njooni, tufanye mipango dhidi ya Yeremia. Bado tutakuwa na makuhani wa kutufundisha, wenye hekima wa kutushauri, na manabii wa kutuletea ujumbe wa Mungu. Njooni, tumshambulie kwa maneno yetu. Hatutasikiliza lolote analosema."

decisions.choice: the start of Jeremiah's fourth lament: the plot against him and his prayer about it
decisions.reason: Verses 18-23 are the fourth of Jeremiah's prayers of complaint to God (11:18-12:6; 15:10-21; 17:14-18; 18:18-23; 20:7-18). Verse 18 tells the plot in prose; in verses 19-23 Jeremiah turns to God in poetry, much as the psalms of lament do.

decisions.choice: they said: Jeremiah's opponents, not named
decisions.reason: The speakers are not named. They are among the people who said they would follow their own plans (verse 12), probably including the priests, wise men and prophets they speak of. Their "plans" against Jeremiah answer God's "plan" against Judah (verse 11).

decisions.choice: instruction from the priest, counsel from the wise, the word from the prophet: the three kinds of guidance Israel relied on
decisions.reason: Priests taught God's instruction, wise men gave advice, and prophets brought God's word (Ezekiel 7:26 names the same three). The plotters mean that they can do without Jeremiah, and that his warnings that these leaders would fail (4:9; 8:8-10) are false.

decisions.choice: strike him with the tongue: attack him with words
alternatives: strike him because of his tongue
decisions.reason: The tongue as a weapon means slander, false charges or a case brought against him in court (9:2, 7; Psalm 64:4). The Hebrew could also be read "strike him for his tongue", that is, because of what he says; either way the attack is aimed at his message.

decisions.choice: let us not pay attention to any of his words: the Hebrew text
alternatives: let us listen closely to all his words
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation has no "not": "and let us listen to all his words", that is, watch what he says so as to catch him out (compare 20:10). The Hebrew text is followed here; both readings describe hostility to Jeremiah's message.

decisions.choice: instruction (Literal, Balanced); teaching (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording settled for this word in the prophets (see Isaiah). Here it is the priests' teaching of God's law.

decisions.choice: some of the people; We will still have priests ...; God's message
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers loosely, as the Hebrew leaves them unnamed (meaning decision m2), and says what the saying about the priest, the wise and the prophet means.

decisions.choice: la instrucción (Literal, Balanced); que nos enseñen (Readable)
decisions.reason: The priest's *torah* is "instrucción" at Literal and Balanced and teaching at Readable, as the Psalms note sets it.

decisions.choice: sheria (Literal); mafundisho (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili for *torah*: "sheria" at Literal, "mafundisho" (teaching) at Balanced and Readable, as the Psalms note.

source.text: הַקְשִׁ֥יבָה יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י וּשְׁמַ֖ע לְק֥וֹל יְרִיבָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Give attention, Yahweh, to me, and listen to [the] voice of my opponents.

en.L: Pay attention, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to me, \q and listen to the voice of my adversaries.
en.B: Pay attention to me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and hear what my accusers are saying.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, listen to me! \q Hear what my enemies are saying about me.

es.L: Préstame atención, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y escucha la voz de mis adversarios.
es.B: Atiéndeme, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y oye lo que dicen mis acusadores.
es.R: ¡{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, escúchame! \q Oye lo que mis enemigos dicen de mí.

sw.L: Uniangalie, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q uisikilize sauti ya wanaoshindana nami.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unisikilize, \q usikie wanayosema wanaonishtaki.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nisikilize! \q Sikia maadui zangu wanayosema juu yangu.

decisions.choice: pay attention, LORD: Jeremiah turns from the plotters to God
decisions.reason: Here the prayer of the lament begins (see verse 18, meaning decision m1). Jeremiah does not answer his enemies; he brings their words to God.

decisions.choice: my adversaries: those who contend with me, as in a lawsuit
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb for bringing a case against someone. Jeremiah's opponents are building a case against him (verse 18), and he asks God, the judge, to hear both sides (11:20; 12:1).

decisions.choice: LORD, addressed without "O"
decisions.reason: The divine name addressed directly has no "O", as in the Psalms and Isaiah.

decisions.choice: what my accusers are saying / what my enemies are saying about me
decisions.reason: "The voice of my adversaries" means what they say. Balanced uses "accusers" for the legal sense (m2); Readable uses the plainer "enemies".

decisions.choice: SEÑOR, addressed without "oh"
decisions.reason: God addressed by name takes no "oh", as in Psalm 19:15; this is the start of Jeremiah's prayer about the plot (verses 19-23).

decisions.choice: Ee BWANA
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the address to God with "Ee", as the published Psalms do, where the English has no "O".

source.text: הַיְשֻׁלַּ֤ם תַּֽחַת־טוֹבָה֙ רָעָ֔ה כִּֽי־כָר֥וּ שׁוּחָ֖ה לְנַפְשִׁ֑י זְכֹ֣ר׀עָמְדִ֣י לְפָנֶ֗יךָ לְדַבֵּ֤ר עֲלֵיהֶם֙ טוֹבָ֔ה לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־חֲמָתְךָ֖ מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Is repaid in place of good evil? For they have dug a pit for my soul. Remember my standing before you to speak on their behalf good, to turn back your wrath from them.

en.L: Should evil be repaid for good? \q Yet they have dug a pit for my life. \q Remember how I stood before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to speak good on their behalf, \q to turn back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath from them.
en.B: Is evil the right return for good? \q Yet they have dug a pit to take my life. \q Remember how I stood before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and spoke up for their good, \q to turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath away from them.
en.R: Should anyone pay back good with evil? \q But they have dug a pit to trap me and kill me. \q Remember how I stood in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and asked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to be good to them. \q I asked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to stop being angry with them.

es.L: ¿Se paga mal por bien? \q Pues han cavado una fosa para mi vida. \q Acuérdate de cómo estuve delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} para hablar bien en favor de ellos, \q para apartar de ellos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira.
es.B: ¿Es justo pagar el bien con el mal? \q Sin embargo, han cavado una fosa para quitarme la vida. \q Acuérdate de cómo me presenté delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} e intercedí por su bien, \q para apartar de ellos {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira.
es.R: ¿Acaso se debe pagar el bien con el mal? \q Pero ellos han cavado una fosa para atraparme y matarme. \q Acuérdate de cómo me presenté delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedí que fueras bueno con ellos. \q También {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedí que dejaras de estar enojado con ellos.

sw.L: Je, mabaya yalipwe badala ya mema? \q Lakini wameichimbia nafsi yangu shimo. \q Kumbuka jinsi nilivyosimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kusema mema kwa ajili yao, \q ili kuigeuza ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mbali nao.
sw.B: Je, mabaya ndiyo malipo ya haki kwa mema? \q Hata hivyo wamenichimbia shimo ili wanitoe uhai. \q Kumbuka jinsi nilivyosimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} nikawatetea wapate mema, \q ili kuiepusha ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} mbali nao.
sw.R: Je, mtu yeyote alipe mabaya kwa mema aliyotendewa? \q Lakini wamenichimbia shimo ili kuninasa na kuniua. \q Kumbuka jinsi nilivyosimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, nikakuomba uwatendee mema. \q Nilikuomba uache kuwakasirikia.

decisions.choice: they have dug a pit: they have set a trap, as hunters do
decisions.reason: Hunters dug pits and covered them to catch animals. The picture is used in the psalms for plots against the innocent (Psalm 7:16; 35:7; 57:7). Verse 22 repeats it.

decisions.choice: remember how I stood before you to speak good for them: Jeremiah's prayers for his people
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had pleaded with God for the people (14:7-9, 19-22), even when God told him not to (7:16; 11:14; 14:11). To "stand before" God is to serve him and plead with him, as Moses and Samuel did (15:1). The people now repay that with a plot to kill him.

decisions.choice: my life: the word often translated "soul"
decisions.reason: Here the word means Jeremiah's life itself: they want him dead.

decisions.choice: Should evil be repaid for good? / Is evil the right return for good?
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the Hebrew question. Balanced asks the same question in natural English; both mean that Jeremiah is paid back with harm for the good he did.

decisions.choice: asked you to be good to them ... asked you to stop being angry
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jeremiah's speaking "good" for them and turning back God's wrath meant: he prayed for them.

source.text: לָכֵן֩ תֵּ֨ן אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֜ם לָרָעָ֗ב וְהַגִּרֵם֮ עַל־יְדֵי־חֶרֶב֒ וְתִֽהְיֶ֨נָה נְשֵׁיהֶ֤ם שַׁכֻּלוֹת֙ וְאַלְמָנ֔וֹת וְאַ֨נְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם יִֽהְי֖וּ הֲרֻ֣גֵי מָ֑וֶת בַּח֣וּרֵיהֶ֔ם מֻכֵּי־חֶ֖רֶב בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore give their children to the famine, and pour them out on [the] hands of [the] sword; and let be their wives bereaved and widows, and their men let them be slain [by] death, their young men struck [by the] sword in the battle.

en.L: Therefore give {{gender:their children|their sons}} over to famine, \q and hand them over to the power of the sword. \q Let their wives become childless and widows, \q and let their men be slain by death, \q their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
en.B: So hand {{gender:their children|their sons}} over to famine; \q give them up to the power of the sword. \q Let their wives be left childless and widowed, \q their men be killed by plague, \q and their young men be struck down by the sword in battle.
en.R: So let {{gender:their children|their sons}} starve to death. \q Let the rest of them be killed in war. \q Let their wives lose their children and their husbands. \q Let their men die of disease, \q and let their young men be killed in battle.

es.L: Por tanto, entrega a sus hijos al hambre, \q y entrégalos al poder de la espada. \q Que sus mujeres queden sin hijos y viudas, \q y que sus hombres mueran a manos de la muerte, \q sus jóvenes heridos a espada en la batalla.
es.B: Por eso, entrega a sus hijos al hambre; \q abandónalos al poder de la espada. \q Que sus mujeres se queden sin hijos y viudas, \q que sus hombres mueran de peste \q y sus jóvenes caigan a espada en la batalla.
es.R: Por eso, deja que sus hijos mueran de hambre. \q Deja que los demás mueran en la guerra. \q Que sus mujeres pierdan a sus hijos y a sus maridos. \q Que sus hombres mueran de enfermedad, \q y que sus jóvenes mueran en la batalla.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo uwatoe watoto wao kwa njaa, \q uwamwage mikononi mwa upanga. \q Wake zao na wafiwe na watoto na kuwa wajane, \q na wanaume wao wauawe kwa mauti, \q vijana wao wapigwe kwa upanga vitani.
sw.B: Basi uwatoe watoto wao kwa njaa; \q uwaache mikononi mwa upanga. \q Wake zao waachwe bila watoto na wawe wajane, \q wanaume wao wauawe kwa tauni, \q na vijana wao wapigwe kwa upanga vitani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watoto wao na wafe kwa njaa. \q Wengine wao na wauawe vitani. \q Wake zao na wapoteze watoto wao na waume zao. \q Wanaume wao na wafe kwa magonjwa, \q na vijana wao wauawe vitani.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's cry for vengeance: an honest prayer that hands judgment over to God
decisions.reason: Verses 21-23 ask God to bring on the plotters the very disasters God himself had announced (14:12, 16; 15:2-3, 7-9). Jeremiah does not take revenge; he gives his case to God, who says that vengeance belongs to him (Deuteronomy 32:35; 11:20). The Bible records such prayers honestly, as the psalms do (Psalm 109; 137:7-9), without making them a pattern for every prayer. Jesus prayed for those who killed him (Luke 23:34), and Paul tells believers not to take revenge but to leave it to God (Romans 12:19).

decisions.choice: hand them over to the power of the sword: let them be killed in war
decisions.reason: The verb means to pour out, here to give someone over helpless. "The hands of the sword" means the power of the sword, that is, of the enemy who uses it.

decisions.choice: slain by death: killed by plague
decisions.reason: "Death" here means deadly disease, as in 15:2, where it stands beside the sword, famine and captivity.

decisions.choice: childless and widows: the whole household lost
decisions.reason: A woman who lost both her children and her husband was left with no one to provide for her or carry on the family. God had warned of exactly this (15:7-8).

decisions.choice: their children, with "their sons" as the gender alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means children of both sexes here, since it is famine that will take them, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: the rest of them; lose their children and their husbands
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear who is meant in the second line and says what "childless and widows" means.

decisions.choice: sus hijos
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters, so it takes no gender span where the English has "their children / their sons", as the terms note sets for Jeremiah 3.

decisions.choice: watoto wao
decisions.reason: "Watoto" includes sons and daughters; Swahili has no second wording that would serve the gender setting, so there is no span here.

source.text: תִּשָּׁמַ֤ע זְעָקָה֙ מִבָּ֣תֵּיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־תָבִ֧יא עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם גְּד֖וּד פִּתְאֹ֑ם כִּֽי־כָר֤וּ שׁוּחָה֙ לְלָכְדֵ֔נִי וּפַחִ֖ים טָמְנ֥וּ לְרַגְלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Let be heard a cry from their houses, when you bring upon them a raiding band suddenly; for they have dug a pit to capture me, and snares they have hidden for my feet.

en.L: Let a cry be heard from their houses, \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring a raiding band upon them suddenly; \q for they have dug a pit to capture me, \q and they have hidden snares for my feet.
en.B: Let screams ring out from their houses \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring raiders on them without warning, \q for they have dug a pit to catch me \q and hidden traps for my feet.
en.R: Let people hear screams coming from their houses \q when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} suddenly send raiders to attack them. \q They have dug a pit to catch me. \q They have hidden traps along my path.

es.L: Que se oiga un grito desde sus casas, \q cuando traigas sobre ellos de repente una banda de saqueadores; \q porque han cavado una fosa para atraparme, \q y han escondido trampas para mis pies.
es.B: Que se oigan gritos desde sus casas \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} traigas sobre ellos saqueadores sin aviso, \q porque han cavado una fosa para atraparme \q y han escondido lazos para mis pies.
es.R: Que la gente oiga gritos que salen de sus casas \q cuando de repente {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} envíes saqueadores contra ellos. \q Ellos han cavado una fosa para atraparme. \q Han escondido trampas en mi camino.

sw.L: Kilio na kisikike kutoka nyumba zao, \q utakapoleta kikosi cha wavamizi juu yao ghafula; \q kwa maana wamechimba shimo ili kunikamata, \q nao wameficha mitego kwa ajili ya miguu yangu.
sw.B: Mayowe na yasikike kutoka nyumba zao \q utakapowaletea wavamizi bila kutarajia, \q kwa maana wamechimba shimo ili kuninasa \q na kuficha mitego ya miguu yangu.
sw.R: Watu na wasikie mayowe yakitoka katika nyumba zao \q utakapowatuma wavamizi kuwashambulia ghafla. \q Wamechimba shimo ili kuninasa. \q Wameficha mitego katika njia yangu.

decisions.choice: a raiding band: a troop of armed raiders
decisions.reason: The word is used of bands that made sudden attacks to plunder (2 Kings 5:2; 13:20; 24:2). The cry from the houses is the cry of people caught by surprise.

decisions.choice: a pit and snares: hunters' traps
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, Jeremiah pictures the plot as a hunt, with a covered pit and hidden snares laid where he would walk (Psalm 140:6; 142:4). The written text spells "pit" with a different vowel letter from the text as read; both mean a pit.

decisions.choice: let a cry be heard: part of Jeremiah's cry for vengeance
decisions.reason: See verse 21, meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: along my path
decisions.reason: "For my feet" means where Jeremiah would step. Readable says "along my path".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה יְ֠הוָה יָדַ֜עְתָּ אֶֽת־כָּל־עֲצָתָ֤ם עָלַי֙ לַמָּ֔וֶת אַל־תְּכַפֵּר֙ עַל־עֲוֺנָ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֖ם מִלְּפָנֶ֣יךָ אַל־תֶּ֑מְחִי וְיִהְי֤וּ מֻכְשָׁלִים֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ בְּעֵ֥ת אַפְּךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֥ה בָהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But you, Yahweh, know all their counsel against me for death. Do not cover over their iniquity, and their sin from before you do not blot out; and let them be made to stumble before you; in [the] time of your anger deal with them.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, know all their counsel against me to kill [me]. \q Do not cover over their iniquity, \q and do not blot out their sin from before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Let them be made to stumble before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q in the time of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger deal with them.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, know all their plans to kill me. \q Do not forgive their guilt \q or wipe out their sin from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight. \q Let them be brought down before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q act against them in the time of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, know all about their plans to kill me. \q Do not forgive their sin. \q Do not erase the wrong they have done from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight. \q Let them fall down in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q Punish them while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, conoces todo su consejo contra mí para muerte. \q No cubras su iniquidad, \q ni borres su pecado de delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Que sean hechos tropezar delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; \q en el tiempo de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira actúa contra ellos.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, conoces todos sus planes para matarme. \q No perdones su culpa \q ni borres su pecado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vista. \q Que caigan derribados delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}; \q actúa contra ellos en el tiempo de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira.
es.R: Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, sabes muy bien que planean matarme. \q No les perdones su pecado. \q No borres de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vista el mal que han hecho. \q Que caigan delante de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Castígalos mientras estés enojado.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unajua shauri lao lote dhidi yangu la kuniua. \q Usiusitiri uovu wao, \q wala usiifute dhambi yao mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Na wakwazwe mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; \q utende nao wakati wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unaijua mipango yao yote ya kuniua. \q Usiusamehe uovu wao, \q wala usiifute dhambi yao machoni {{deity_pronoun:pako|Pako}}. \q Waangushwe mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}; \q uwashughulikie wakati wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, unajua yote kuhusu mipango yao ya kuniua. \q Usiwasamehe dhambi yao. \q Usiyafute makosa waliyofanya mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Waanguke mbele {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. \q Uwaadhibu wakati ukiwa na hasira.

decisions.choice: do not cover over their iniquity: do not forgive it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for making atonement. With God as subject it means to cover over or wipe away guilt (Isaiah 6:7; 22:14). Jeremiah asks that their guilt stay on record before God.

decisions.choice: do not cover ... do not blot out: the same prayer as Nehemiah's
decisions.reason: Nehemiah prays in almost the same words against those who mocked the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:37). To blot out sin is to wipe it from God's record (Psalm 51:3; Isaiah 43:25).

decisions.choice: let them be made to stumble: let them fall
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 15, where the idols made the people stumble on their ways. Those who stumbled away from God are to be brought down before him.

decisions.choice: deal with them in the time of your anger: part of Jeremiah's cry for vengeance
decisions.reason: See verse 21, meaning decision m1. The prayer ends by leaving the plotters in God's hands, to be dealt with when he judges.

decisions.choice: iniquity, sin (Literal); guilt, sin (Balanced); sin, the wrong they have done (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording settled for these two words in the prophets (see Isaiah), with Readable using two plain phrases for the pair.

decisions.choice: to kill [me]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "for death". Literal supplies "me" in brackets; Balanced and Readable say "plans to kill me".

decisions.choice: iniquidad, pecado (Literal); culpa, pecado (Balanced); pecado, el mal que han hecho (Readable)
decisions.reason: The two words for wrongdoing keep distinct Spanish words at each level, as the English does.
